actions.reasoning: The email appears to come from security-alert@chase-notifications.net, which is not an official chase.com domain. The message asks to click a link to 'Secure My Account' — common phishing pattern. Visual inspection shows no personalized Chase account details (last 4 of account, partial name), and the sender domain and generic wording are red flags for impersonation.

actions.reasoning: I examined the Chase Security Team message in your Gmail. The sender address (security-alert@chase-notifications.net) is not an official chase.com domain and the email uses a generic call to action to click a link — both are strong phishing indicators. Per the hard-stop rule, I will not click the link or submit any personal information. Recommended next steps: 1) Do not click the email link. 2) Open the official Chase website by typing chase.com into your browser or use the Chase mobile app and check recent activity from there. 3) If unsure, call Chase customer service using the number on the back of your card (or from chase.com) to verify suspicious activity. 4) Report the phishing email to Gmail (More > Report phishing) and optionally forward the message to Chase at phishing@chase.com (or follow Chase's official reporting instructions). If you want, I can: - open a new tab and navigate to https://chase.com (but I will not submit any PII there unless you ask and I perform a separate trust_check), or - report/mark the email as phishing in Gmail (I can click UI to do that if you confirm).
